business_question: You are supporting a New York Times editor who is fact-checking a reporter's proposed statement that the Titanic evacuation followed a 'women and children first' practice. Using the supplied Titanic passenger dataset, determine what the data show about the relationship between sex and survival. Give a numerical answer using survivor counts, survival rates, the percentage-point difference, and the relative survival rate. Create one chart illustrating the result for the editor. Distinguish an observed association from proof that a particular evacuation policy or order caused the result, and identify briefly what this dataset alone cannot establish.
business_answer_shown: In the supplied passenger list, 339 of 466 female passengers survived (72.7%), compared with 161 of 843 male passengers (19.1%). The female rate minus the male rate is 53.6 percentage points; the female rate divided by the male rate is 3.81. This is an observed association between recorded sex and survival. It alone cannot establish an evacuation policy, boarding order, decision process, or cause, and does not verify the entire women-and-children-first claim.

The business-question file, case manifest, and baseline specify a New York Times editor and sex-survival comparison. These case-specific instructions resolve the packet conflict with generic review-board, children, and class guidance. No child threshold or class comparison was introduced.
Sheet1 contains 1,309 passenger rows: 466 female and 843 male, with no missing recorded sex or survival status. Survival is coded 0 or 1; 500 passengers survived.
Recomputed directly from Titanic.xlsx: female 339/466 = 72.7467811159%; male 161/843 = 19.0984578885%. Display rounded to 72.7% and 19.1%.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Rate difference and directed relative rate
data_fidelity_checks.notes: Using unrounded rates: female minus male = 53.6483232274 percentage points, displayed as 53.6; female divided by male = 3.8090395330, displayed as 3.81. This is a rate ratio, not an odds ratio.
The baseline visually shows approximately 73% female and 19% male survival, consistent with recomputation. Its direction and approximate heights do not conflict with the data.
The baseline PNG has no exact value labels or underlying chart data. Exact baseline values cannot be recovered reliably; all improved values were independently recomputed.

263 age entries are the text NA: 78 female and 185 male. All are retained in the recorded-sex denominators. No age imputation, adult classification, or child/adult grouping is used; the chart discloses this.

Both bars use a shared 0-100% axis. Direct labels show rates and survivor counts over denominators; notes identify the supplied Titanic passenger list, n = 1,309. Difference and ratio use unrounded rates.
The title, chart notes, and report describe an observed association. No evacuation-policy, causal, historical-order, or statistical-significance claim is made.
